name: showreel-48-has-parent
style: Three tall add-on tiles on a phone, every box ticked and every tile dull grey-plum: each tile flickers toward lit and dies on every bug beat with a red outline flash, the finger unticks and reticks a box and nothing reacts (LIT 0), then one CSS line, .card:has(input:checked), and the tiles light by themselves (black look, a violet accent).

voice.text: Why won't the card light up? The box is ticked, but CSS can't select a parent. The fix: card has checked. Now the card lights itself. One line, no JavaScript.

caption:
Still toggling a class in JavaScript to light up a card? Yes or no. 🟣

Tick a checkbox and the card stays dull, because CSS could not select a parent. :has() changes that. MDN: it represents an element if any of the relative selectors passed to it match, a way of selecting a parent element. The fix: .card:has(input:checked) styles the whole card when its checkbox is on. Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4 (MDN browser compatibility); Baseline widely available.

Watch the counter: LIT reads 0 while 3 boxes are ticked, then 3 after the fix, and it drops to 2 the moment you untick a box.

Comment yes or no, and send it to whoever still toggles that class.

sources.note: MDN :has() (page source mdn/content, read 26 Nov 2026): represents an element if any of the relative selectors passed as an argument match at least one element when anchored against this element; a way of selecting a parent element or a previous sibling element; Baseline widely available since December 2023
MDN BCD css.selectors.has (read 26 Nov 2026): Chrome 105, Edge 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4

tip.title: Why won't the card light up when you tick its checkbox?
tip.why: CSS selectors used to stop at the element itself, so a card could not react to the checkbox inside it and pages added JavaScript to toggle a class. :has() represents an element if any of the relative selectors passed to it match (MDN: a way of selecting a parent element), so .card:has(input:checked) styles the whole card when its checkbox is checked. Supported in Chrome 105, Firefox 121 and Safari 15.4 (MDN browser compatibility data).
tip.code:
<label class="card">
  <input type="checkbox"> Oat milk
</label>

/* the card lights when its box is ticked */
.card:has(input:checked) { background: violet; }

experiment.change: a myth that changed (CSS can't select a parent) shown as three ticked boxes with dull cards, LIT 0 against TICKED 3, then one :has() line lights the cards and a card dims the moment its box is unticked; black look with a violet accent (new hue), a small push and pull, the reel loops into frame 0
